state: We are conducting a documentation-only stress review of a Can testing architecture; code trials and implementation are outside this round. AI coding agents are the authors, with full normal Can functions controlling test steps, comparisons, run decisions and reporting. No handwritten host-language scenario harness may survive migration. Execution presently chosen is Can-to-TypeScript on Bun, where a qualified reference R compiles the judge, C denotes candidate artifacts under examination, and an external Go supervisor N owns constrained resources and fresh workers. The host has a 256 GB disk, bounded load and pre-effect cleanup ownership; disposable builds cannot become persistent private bundles or caches. Existing native qualification and runtime suites inspect JSON token spelling, integers outside JS's safe range, signed-zero representation, hostile accessors and proxies including revoked ones, absence of thenable reads, reference/error-occurrence identity, and late loser faults or leases. Admitted operations come from a closed typed catalogue. The emitter normally represents a named Can callback as an asynchronous closure returning Promise<Completion<T>>; special value/invokeSync paths exist but do not establish a general synchronous getter/trap compiler contract. Opaque per-session handles and exact tagged observations avoid resolving raw thenables in transport. Output launch verifies the generation's runtime identity and private runtime hashes; substituting C modules into an R probe is therefore not a supported bridge. Observations about Bun APIs, execution of R observer code and behavior of C adapters need separately recorded provenance, and candidate imports are forbidden in the trusted judge. Reviewed immediate fault descriptors can construct common synchronous hostile values without embedding scripts, although a same-realm ingress to C production adapters still lacks qualification. Browser grid cases intercept and hold requests, separate server contact from delayed/corrupt delivery, replay an operation ID and capture delayed callback errors. The proposed browser service supplies paused tokens with one-shot fetch and resolution plus capped events and terminal draining, leaving choices in Can and exposing no JavaScript evaluation escape hatch. Whether the round trip and final callback seal work remains open. F02/F03 SQL sources combine candidate Can runtime calls with direct Bun SQL queries: contention and lock modes SKIP LOCKED/NOWAIT with 55P03, poisoned transactions with 25P02 and later replay, RETURNING and row cardinality, exact int64/money/timestamps/JSON, eight or sixteen writers, SQLite and optional MySQL. This separate query path bypasses Can SQL adapters but shares Bun SQL. Session-affine transactions, raw exact results, native failures and unknown commits must survive the new observer without automatic write replay; pooled stateless query calls do not establish affinity. The CLI launch tests deliberately feed hostile NODE_OPTIONS/BUN_OPTIONS into the candidate Go launcher, expecting its Bun child to have sanitized startup while fd 3 carries the original application snapshot. Preserve those adversarial inputs only for C, keep R/N isolated, and distinguish direct-entry startup with sanitized environment, fd 3 ending in EOF, stdin bytes and fd 4 output lease. Small future trials must establish blocked-writer cancellation, unused snapshots and child lease retention after its launcher terminates. None of this source evidence establishes working replacement APIs. Every retained ledger facet needs Can-authored assertions, deliberate failing controls and confirmed cleanup before deleting its host harness; a small feasibility success establishes only its stated mechanism. Further inspected details: the browser driver must answer route operations during an unsettled click; a pair of same-task DOM clicks cannot be replaced by separate round trips. Needed bindings include a finite typed synchronous action batch, clone/remount with identity, correctly ordered defaultPrevented event observation, page-realm credential/CSP-aware Fetch and browser Can codec data exports. None permits a foreign scenario program. A remote Firefox service is shared, so cleanup owns only the acquired context and connection. In SQL, F02 observes locks via runtime participants, not an independent raw lock check. Current RETURNING checker/runtime support outdates F03's future-work comment. The poison scenario writes nothing successfully before the duplicate: a sentinel plus independent post-settlement read would add evidence for rollback. A SQL budget expiry leaves native work running; commit_unknown needs settlement and an activity fence before a fresh raw read has meaning, or the effect stays unresolved. Historical cold-pool handling may have been superseded by the current callback-binding fix. Legacy fixed table naming and ignored cleanup exceptions are inadequate resource-ownership mechanisms.

native_bridge_priority.instructions: Given the observed runtime and callback boundaries, what should be the initial native-test bridge strategy?

criteria.explicit_bridge: Retain current execution, distinguish raw runtime from candidate-adapter evidence, and demonstrate scoped value transport plus small immediate fault forms and reviewed C ingress before expanding synchronous callback bindings. Preserve full ordinary functions in the suite.
criteria.general_sync_first: Make a broad compiler-supported synchronous callback path the first prerequisite for these native suites, with ordinary Can supplying trap behavior and native construction limited to representation mechanics.
criteria.interpreter_first: First investigate a complete Can IR executor offering direct synchronous host callbacks, keeping N external and preserving ordinary functions, before extending the current compiled bridge.

browser_control_location.instructions: Select the first browser route-callback execution model to qualify for these observed scenarios.

criteria.tokens_to_can: Start with the proposed token exchange to ordinary Can, separate server contact from response release, and qualify deferred decisions and draining before introducing a second Can callback execution location.
criteria.local_can_callback: Place reference-compiled Can handlers alongside the browser driver from the outset and keep final assertions in the worker; qualify that local artifact/binding path instead of worker token decisions.
criteria.both_initially: Qualify remote token control and local R-built handlers together before browser migration, giving each scenario an explicit execution-location choice.

database_observer.instructions: Choose the initial database observer for the adapter-focused obligations described in state.

criteria.raw_driver_scoped: Expose session-affine raw Bun SQL actions and exact errors/results under separate ownership, explicitly limiting independence to bypassing the Can adapter and adding a different observer for lower-driver claims.
criteria.cli_default: Make separate database client executables the initial observation path for all these cases, implementing persistent sessions and typed framing rather than depending on raw Bun SQL.
criteria.dual_every_case: Initially qualify all database obligations through two independent client paths, retaining direct Bun access and an additional driver even where the tested layer is only Can.
